topics.topic: PT Tower Bersama Infrastructure Rp2.37 trillion bonds and sukuk issuance
topics.known_state: TBIG will issue Continuous Bonds Phase VII Phase V Year 2026 worth Rp1.24 trillion and Continuous Ijarah Sukuk Phase I Phase V worth Rp1.13 trillion, offering October 9-12, 2026 and listing on the IDX on October 16, 2026. Bonds have three series with coupons of 7.15%, 7.65%, and 7.80% per year and tenors of 370 days, three years, and five years; the sukuk offers equivalent yields with matching tenors. Proceeds will repay the entire Rp1.95 trillion UOB Indonesia loan maturing October 19, 2026 and Rp408.89 billion of a Rp421 billion Bank Mizuho Indonesia loan, with the remaining Rp12.91 billion covered by operating cash flow.

topics.topic: PT Pelayaran Nasional Bina Buana Raya purchase of AHTS vessel MP Maverick
topics.known_state: BBRM purchased the AHTS vessel MP Maverick (80T BP AHTS, 6,000 BHP) from Great Union China Limited for US$12.1 million (approximately Rp214.8 billion), with the purchase agreement disclosed to the IDX on September 30, 2026. KJPP Rengganis, Hamid & Rekan valued the vessel at Rp230.91 billion (US$13,006,872), with appraisal dates reported variously as 28 September 2026 and 18 September 2026 at Rp17,753 per US dollar. The transaction equals 31.8% of BBRM's US$38 million equity and required no shareholder approval as the seller is not affiliated; funding includes a Rp120 billion (about US$7.26 million) investment loan from PT Bank IBK Indonesia Tbk. The vessel has been received and is ready to operate.

topics.topic: PT Merdeka Gold Resources Rp6.45 trillion affiliate loan facility to PT Pani Industri Nusantara
topics.known_state: EMAS and subsidiaries PT Gorontalo Sejahtera Mining and PT Puncak Emas Tani Sejahtera disbursed an unsecured affiliate loan facility totaling Rp6.45 trillion to PT Pani Industri Nusantara, operator of the Pani gold mine in Pohuwato, Gorontalo (facility provision dated September 25, 2026 in one report). EMAS provided Rp3.05 trillion and GSM and PETS each Rp1.70 trillion, with interest at the INDONIA benchmark rate plus a 1.70% annual margin and a term through December 31, 2031. The facility exceeds 20% of EMAS's equity as of June 30, 2026, qualifying as a material transaction under OJK rules, but requires no shareholder approval as each transaction is below 50% of total equity and occurs within one group.

topics.topic: PT AirAsia Indonesia plan to repair negative equity via share issuance and payable restructuring
topics.known_state: CMPP is evaluating a rights issue (PMHMETD) or private placement (PMTHMETD) and restructuring trade payables and lease liabilities to its controlling entity and/or shareholders into semi-equity instruments to repair negative equity and address its suspended shares. As of June 30, 2026, equity attributable to owners of the parent was negative Rp12.19 trillion, with total liabilities of Rp16.91 trillion against total assets of Rp4.73 trillion. H1 2026 revenue fell 1.79% to Rp3.91 trillion, operating loss widened to Rp922.27 billion, and net loss rose to Rp1.45 trillion, pressured by a 26.1% increase in fuel costs to Rp1.99 trillion and foreign exchange losses.

topics.topic: Daaz Bara Lestari and HYD Investment framework agreement with Aneka Tambang and IBC for US$6 billion EV battery facility
topics.known_state: PT Daaz Bara Lestari Tbk (DAAZ), through consortium partner HYD Investment Limited, signed a framework agreement with PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and Indonesia Battery Corporation (IBC) to develop an EV battery facility targeting 20 GWh capacity with US$6 billion in investment. DAAZ has been identified as a strategic partner of ANTM in the nickel downstream project.

topics.topic: Daaz Bara Lestari contracts from Aneka Tambang and PT Gag Nikel
topics.known_state: DAAZ secured a Rp1.1 trillion three-year contract from ANTM for hauling, development, and loading at UPBN Konut, Southeast Sulawesi, plus a Rp3.95 billion 12-month contract from ANTM subsidiary PT Gag Nikel for reclamation of Gag Island and Raja Ampat.

topics.topic: PT City Retail Developments divestment of seven warehouse and logistics subsidiaries for Rp1.3 trillion
topics.known_state: NIRO is divesting 100% ownership in seven warehouse rental and logistics subsidiaries (PT Cella Management Logistik, PT Cella Argya Logistik, PT Bukit Inti Lestari, PT CRE BIL Indonesia, PT Cella Cakra Logistik, PT Cella Emerald Logistik, PT Cella Gemilang Logistik) valued at Rp1.3 trillion to Singapore-based Nusantara Logistics Investments Pte. Ltd., generating a divestment gain of Rp201.3 billion. Based on June 30, 2026 financials, cash rises from Rp1.2 trillion to Rp2.3 trillion and the current-period loss improves from Rp237.5 billion to Rp36.2 billion. The buyer is not affiliated with the selling entities.

topics.topic: Telkom Indonesia board of directors and commissioners reshuffle at RUPSLB
topics.known_state: At a RUPSLB in Jakarta on September 30, 2026, TLKM shareholders dismissed Dian Siswarini as President Director, replacing her with Nanang Hendarno (previously Director of Network since June 2025). IT & Digital Director Faizal Rochmad Djoemadi was removed, with Kharim I.G. Siregar appointed; Budi Satria Dharma Purba moved to Director of Network and Radita Ali Putra to Director of Wholesale & International Service. The new board includes Veranita Yosephine, Willy Saelan, Arthur Angelo Syailendra, Seno Soemadji, and Andy Kelana as directors, with Angga Raka Prabowo as President Commissioner.

topics.topic: Telkom Indonesia second-phase fiber network spin-off to InfraNexia
topics.known_state: TLKM shareholders approved the second-phase spin-off of the Wholesale Fiber Connectivity business into PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia (InfraNexia), completed on September 30, 2026. InfraNexia took over management of 90% of network infrastructure assets; the second phase was valued at Rp49.9 trillion, complementing the first phase of Rp35.8 trillion for a total spin-off value of Rp85.7 trillion. Assets span approximately 112,000 km of fiber optic network, including 26,000 km of domestic submarine cable (SKKL), across 4 areas, 12 regions, and 61 districts.

topics.topic: Astra Agro Lestari interim dividend of Rp233 per share for fiscal year 2026
topics.known_state: AALI will distribute an interim dividend of Rp233 per share for fiscal year 2026, totaling Rp449.03 billion, about 40.9% of its net profit of Rp1.09 trillion for the period ended June 30, 2026, approved September 29, 2026 and disclosed to the IDX on September 30, 2026. Cum dividend date is October 8, 2026 and ex-dividend October 9, 2026 (regular and negotiation markets), cum and ex dates of October 12 and 13, 2026 in the cash market, recording date October 12, 2026, and payment on October 26, 2026. For fiscal year 2025, AALI paid an interim dividend of Rp123 per share totaling Rp236.73 billion.

topics.topic: Astra Graphia Rp297 per share dividend changed from planned interim to final cash dividend
topics.known_state: ASGR announced a Rp297 per share dividend decided by its Board of Directors on September 25, 2026, with cum dividend dates of October 7, 2026 (regular and negotiation markets) and October 9, 2026 (cash market), ex-dividend dates of October 8 and October 12 respectively, and a recording date of October 9, 2026 at 16:00 WIB. The company changed the planned interim dividend of Rp400.05 billion into a final cash dividend of Rp297 per share, to be paid from retained earnings of prior fiscal years, requiring shareholder approval at a RUPSLB planned for November 2026, after which a new payment schedule will be announced, replacing the previously set payment date of October 26, 2026.

topics.topic: Golden Energy Mines US$200 million interim dividend for fiscal year 2026
topics.known_state: GEMS will distribute an interim dividend for fiscal year 2026 totaling US$200 million, equal to US$0.034 per share (Rp611.93 per share at the Bank Indonesia mid-rate, with exchange rates stated variously as Rp17,998 and Rp17,996 per US dollar; one article puts the total at about Rp3.58 trillion across 5.88 billion shares, another Rp3.57 trillion at Rp17,877 per USD or Rp607.82 per share). Board of commissioners approval was dated September 29, 2026, and the dividend represents 90.92% of net profit of US$219.96 million attributable to the parent entity based on data as of September 25, 2026. Cum dividend dates are October 8, 2026 (regular and negotiation) and October 12, 2026 (cash), ex-dividend October 9 and 13, recording date October 12, 2026 until 4:00 PM WIB, and payment on October 22, 2026. Foreign shareholders without tax treaty documentation face 20% withholding tax under Article 26.

topics.topic: PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas planned rights issue of up to 15 billion shares
topics.known_state: VKTR plans a rights issue of up to 15 billion new shares at an exercise price of Rp200 per share, potentially raising up to Rp3 trillion to expand its commercial electric vehicle ecosystem, including vehicle procurement, working capital, and e-MaaS.

topics.topic: Bukit Asam Rp6 trillion credit facilities from BRI and Bank Mandiri backed by DHE SDA deposits
topics.known_state: PTBA obtained financing facilities totaling Rp6 trillion signed on September 23 and 28, 2026: a Rp2 trillion working capital credit from Bank Rakyat Indonesia and a Rp4 trillion bridging loan from Bank Mandiri, both using Export Proceeds of Natural Resources (DHE SDA) funds as underlying collateral placed at Himbara banks. The total facility exceeds 20% of PTBA's equity based on financial statements as of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026, making it a material transaction.

topics.topic: RR Capital Group sale of Panca Global Kapital shares worth Rp29.64 billion
topics.known_state: RR Capital Group Pte Ltd, PEGE's largest shareholder, sold 156 million shares at Rp190 per share on September 28, 2026, raising Rp29.64 billion, reducing its stake from 42.41% to 38.28% of voting rights. Ultimate Beneficial Owner Trisno Limanto holds an aggregate 18.94%, and PEGE's public free float was 29.74% as of end-August 2026.

topics.topic: PT Indonesia Kendaraan Terminal agreement ending Maspion Terminal operations cooperation for Rp13.78 billion
topics.known_state: IPCC signed a sale and purchase binding agreement (PPJB) with PT Maspion Industrial Estate to end its cooperation agreement over Maspion Terminal operations in Gresik, East Java, valued at Rp13.78 billion, payable by PT Maspion Industrial Estate after all PPJB conditions are met. The transaction is not material under POJK No. 17/2020 as it does not exceed 20% of the company's equity. The terminal, developed since a 2014 strategic partnership, is the first modern vehicle terminal in East Java serving RoRo cargo.

topics.topic: PT Japfa Comfeed divestment of PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara for Rp1.807 trillion
topics.known_state: JPFA, together with PT Ciomas Adisatwa, sold all 31,000 shares (100%) of PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara for Rp1.807 trillion to Japfa Pte. Ltd. and Bionovus Pte. Ltd., affiliates within the Japfa Group, under a share purchase agreement signed September 29, 2026. Japfa Pte. Ltd. is JPFA's controlling shareholder with a 56.34% stake, and Bionovus is 100% owned by Japfa Pte. Ltd. Valuation used KJPP RSR appraisal as of June 30, 2026 via DCF-FCFF and GPTC methods. JPFA loses direct control of the animal health and vaccine business and will no longer consolidate Vaksindo and its subsidiaries in India and Vietnam, while commercial supply arrangements continue on substantially the same terms.

topics.topic: Garuda Indonesia H1-2026 financial results
topics.known_state: GIAA posted first-half 2026 revenue of US$1.80 billion (Rp32.1 trillion), up 16% year-on-year, cutting its net loss 23.2% to US$113 million from US$147.1 million. Scheduled flights contributed US$1.31 billion (+10.9%), non-scheduled flights rose 32.5% to US$272.8 million driven by hajj transport revenue of US$232.2 million (+51.6%), and other revenue rose 32.2% to US$209.2 million. EBIT was US$74.0 million (+12.7%) and EBITDA US$431.6 million (+5.8%); fuel costs jumped 43.6% to US$677.6 million, finance expenses fell 11.6% to US$222.4 million following debt repayments after Danantara's Rp23.67 trillion capital injection in late 2025, the fleet reached 104 aircraft by June 2026, and the equity deficit narrowed to US$52.2 million from US$1.5 billion a year earlier.

topics.topic: Indonesia Stock Exchange limited short selling launch for five large-cap stocks
topics.known_state: The IDX implemented limited short selling for five LQ45 large-cap stocks starting October 1, 2026: ASII, BBCA, BRPT, BUMI, and INDF, in line with OJK Regulation Number 6 of 2024. Exchange members PT Semesta Indovest Sekuritas (MG) and PT Ajaib Sekuritas Asia (XC) serve the transactions. Eligible investors must have held an RDN/regular securities account for at least six months, register with a participating securities firm, and have a minimum of Rp50 million in initial capital, with short selling capped at 0.02% of outstanding shares. An earlier IDX study estimated the scheme could boost liquidity by up to 17% assuming five exchange members participate.

topics.topic: PT Surya Madistrindo independent director resignation
topics.known_state: SRSN announced the resignation of Independent Director Sharad Ganesh Ugrankar on September 30, 2026, which the company said has no material impact pending RUPSLB approval.

topics.topic: Bank Central Asia denial of Haji Isam acquisition rumor
topics.known_state: BBCA management, responding to an IDX request for clarification, confirmed that social media rumors that BCA was to be acquired by Haji Isam were untrue and urged the public to rely on official sources.

topics.topic: Garuda Indonesia PMHMETD III rights issue plan with Danantara inbreng of GMFI shares
topics.known_state: GIAA plans a limited public offering with pre-emptive rights (PMHMETD III) as part of its restructuring program. PT Danantera Asset Management (DAM), holding 370,902,553,959 shares, will exercise its rights through an inbreng of GMFI shares worth Rp5.66 trillion, obtained from InJourney following the land inbreng of PT Angkasa Pura into PT Garuda Maintenance Facility Aero Asia Tbk (GMFI). The rights issue will issue up to 124,352,806,609 Series E shares with a nominal value of Rp25 per share, with remaining proceeds used as working capital. A RUPSLB to discuss the plan is scheduled for November 6, 2026.

topics.topic: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa audited H1-2026 results
topics.known_state: DSSA reported audited H1-2026 net profit attributable to owners of the parent of US$174.35 million, up 79.5% from US$97.08 million in H1-2025. Revenue rose about 34% to US$1.77 billion, driven mainly by coal mining and trading (US$1.53 billion from US$1.18 billion) and cable TV and internet services (US$170.49 million from US$87.15 million). Gross profit grew around 34% to US$641.23 million; total assets increased to US$6.07 billion from US$4.41 billion, and liabilities rose to US$3.02 billion from US$2.15 billion, primarily from long-term bank loans.

topics.topic: Satu Visi Putra transformation into a healthcare holding company
topics.known_state: At a RUPSLB, PT Satu Visi Putra Tbk shareholders approved a transformation into a healthcare holding company, including acquiring 72.91% of PT Hasna Medika Bakti Cirebon (HMBC) for about Rp319 billion and a private placement of up to 307.5 million new shares (10% of paid-in capital).

topics.topic: United Tractors interim dividend payment rescheduled to November 2026
topics.known_state: UNTR changed its interim dividend payment date from October 26, 2026 to November 2026, intending to use financial statements as of September 30, 2026 as the basis for the distribution. The dividend amount remains unchanged at up to Rp1,478 trillion, equivalent to Rp430 per share, with the new schedule to be announced after the September financial report is published.

topics.topic: PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas H1-2026 results and e-MaaS business model
topics.known_state: VKTR reported H1-2026 net sales of Rp648 billion, up 56% year on year, with operating profit up 1,782% to Rp15 billion and net profit up 25% to Rp10 billion, driven by commercial electric vehicle sales and parts manufacturing. The company is developing an Electric Mobility-as-a-Service (e-MaaS) model shifting vehicle usage costs from capital expenditure to operational expenditure through periodic lease payments, targeting sectors including public transport, logistics, plantations, industry, and mining.

topics.topic: Sarana Menara Nusantara Rp500 billion share buyback
topics.known_state: TOWR will repurchase up to 1.18 billion shares, about 2% of its issued and paid-up capital, using internal funds of up to Rp500 billion excluding transaction fees, from September 30 to December 30, 2026, with PT BCA Sekuritas as broker, and may end early if the cost or share target is met. The company stated the move aims to support the stock price.

topics.topic: ESDM Ministerial Decree 365.K/MB.01/MEM.B/2026 tightening use of affiliates in mining services
topics.known_state: Indonesia's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources issued Decree Number 365.K/MB.01/MEM.B/2026, signed by Bahlil Lahadalia, requiring holders of IUP and IUPK permits to obtain ministerial approval before assigning mining services work to subsidiaries and affiliates, with exceptions for government assignments, national strategic projects, processing and refining facilities, coal development, and domestic supply.

topics.topic: Waskita Beton Precast delayed bond coupon payments and PEFINDO idB rating with Negative outlook
topics.known_state: WSBP received a 90-day remedial period to resolve the delayed payment of the 8th coupon on Obligasi I Tahun 2022 and Obligasi II Tahun 2022, which fell due on September 25, 2026, due to insufficient Cash Flow Available for Debt Service (CFADS). PEFINDO affirmed its idB rating with a Negative outlook on September 30, 2026, stating the shortfall does not constitute a default because the homologation agreement permits deferred obligations to be settled based on CFADS availability, but warned it will downgrade if WSBP fails to pay within the 90-day deadline or if creditors cancel the homologation agreement.

topics.topic: DSSA H1 2026 financial results
topics.known_state: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) reported H1 2026 net profit of US$174.35 million (also stated as US$174.4 million, around Rp2.9 trillion), up 79.6% from US$79.08 million a year earlier, on revenue of US$1.77 billion, up 34%. Coal mining and trading contributed US$1.53 billion (up 29.78%), cable TV and internet grew 95.62% to US$170.49 million, renewables posted US$176,971 (up 153.91%), and the digital segment posted Q1 revenue of US$69.1 million (up 50%) plus digital solutions and data center revenues of US$6.63 million and US$5.05 million. MoraRepublic's fiber-to-the-home network reached 186 cities and regencies, and SM+ with Korea Investment Real Asset Management and LG Sinar Mas is completing the SMX01 AI data center in Jakarta targeted to begin operations in Q4 2026.

topics.topic: DSSA acquisition of PT Bali Media Telekomunikasi
topics.known_state: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) completed the acquisition of PT Bali Media Telekomunikasi (BMT), which holds a 24.57% stake in PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk (EXCL), giving DSSA indirect ownership in EXCL as part of its telecommunications and digital infrastructure expansion.

topics.topic: Garuda Indonesia jumbo rights issue (PMHMETD III) with Danantara GMFI share injection
topics.known_state: PT Garuda Indonesia Tbk (GIAA) plans a jumbo rights issue of up to 124,352,806,609 Series E shares at Rp25 nominal value as part of its 2025-2029 financial restructuring. PT Danantara Asset Management will participate via an inbreng of 82,100,173,900 GMFI shares (65.77% of GMFI's placed and paid-up capital) valued at Rp5.66 trillion (one report states Rp5,664 trillion); the shares will transfer from PT Angkasa Pura Indonesia to InJourney and then to DAM via a non-cash dividend in specie before DAM exercises its rights non-cash while others may exercise in cash. The plan requires shareholder approval at an RUPSLB on 6 November 2026 with results announced 10 November 2026, and OJK effectiveness within 12 months; the exercise price will be set in the prospectus. Proceeds will fund GIAA's acquisition of GMFI shares and working capital for its 2026 stabilization and recovery plan, with the injection expected to improve consolidated equity to negative US$52.15 million and standalone equity to US$646.15 million by 30 June 2026.

topics.topic: Garuda Indonesia H1 2026 financial results and negative equity
topics.known_state: PT Garuda Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (GIAA) reported H1 2026 revenue of US$1.80 billion, up 16.0% YoY, with net loss narrowed 23.2% to US$113.0 million from US$147.1 million. Scheduled flights contributed US$1.31 billion, non-scheduled flights rose 32.5% to US$272.8 million (including hajj transport revenue of US$232.2 million), and other revenue including MRO rose 32.2% to US$209.2 million; jet fuel costs rose 43.6% to US$677.6 million. As of 30 June 2026, equity attributable to owners was negative US$163.0 million (vs negative US$39.3 million at end-2025), total equity was negative US$52.2 million after positive equity of US$44.4 million in FY2025 and US$68.2 million in Q1-2026; total liabilities fell to US$7.4 billion, total debt fell 4.0% to US$3.76 billion, the fleet returned to 104 operational aircraft, operating cash flow was positive at US$253.1 million, and cash and equivalents stood at US$624.3 million.

topics.topic: Morgan Stanley increases stake in GoTo (GOTO)
topics.known_state: Morgan Stanley and Co International Plc bought 400 million GOTO shares at Rp27 on September 18, 2026, worth Rp10.8 billion, raising its stake from 6.9951% (80.54 billion shares) to 7.0299% (80.94 billion shares) as a non-controlling shareholder.

topics.topic: United Tractors new share buyback program October-December 2026
topics.known_state: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) announced a share buyback with a maximum allocation of Rp2 trillion, running from October 1 to December 31, 2026, executed on the IDX via one appointed securities company and funded by internal cash, in line with POJK No. 13/2023, OJK Letter No. S-112/D.04/2026, and POJK No. 29/2023. Purchases will not exceed 20% of issued and paid-up capital and will keep free float at no less than 15% (one report states free float after the buyback will be below 15%); repurchased shares will be held as treasury shares and the program may end early. Based on 30 June 2026 consolidated financials, the buyback would reduce total assets from Rp179.1 trillion to Rp177.1 trillion and total equity from Rp101.8 trillion to Rp99.8 trillion, while EPS would rise from Rp271 to Rp277. Context: UNTR's H1 2026 revenue fell 15% YoY to Rp58.3 trillion and net profit before non-recurring items fell 48% to Rp4.3 trillion.

topics.topic: United Tractors completion of prior share buyback (July-September 2026)
topics.known_state: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) completed its share buyback period running from 1 July 2026 to 30 September 2026, repurchasing 57,974,100 shares for Rp1.42 trillion out of the Rp2 trillion allocated.

topics.topic: United Tractors interim dividend payment rescheduled to November 2026
topics.known_state: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) rescheduled its interim dividend payment, originally set for 26 October 2026, to November 2026, keeping the amount unchanged at Rp1.47 trillion, or Rp430 per share, based on financial statements as of 30 September 2026.

topics.topic: Indah Prakasa Sentosa (INPS) loan and acquisition of PT Tri Satria Indah Motor
topics.known_state: PT Indah Prakasa Sentosa Tbk (INPS) received a Rp6 billion loan facility from Charli Handaka under an agreement dated 30 September 2026 with a one-year term, to fund the acquisition of shares in PT Tri Satria Indah Motor, which will become a subsidiary consolidated at a 90% ownership portion. The target has secured a three-wheeled motor vehicle procurement project worth around Rp1.25 trillion from an entity within the Danantara group with an estimated margin of 7% to 8%. INPS, whose shareholders include PT Graha Inti Guna Persada (65.86%), Andry Hakim (10.02%), and the public (24.12%), is diversifying into the automotive sector and is also conducting a limited public offering (PMTHMETD) of up to 1,250,000,000 new shares at Rp100 nominal and exercise price.

topics.topic: Yancoal Australia acquisition of Kestrel Coal Group and Adaro Andalan (AADI) full divestment
topics.known_state: Yancoal Australia completed on October 1, 2026 its US$1.85 billion cash acquisition of Kestrel Coal Group Pty Ltd, which holds an 80% stake in the Kestrel underground longwall metallurgical coal mine in Bowen Basin, Queensland, after PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI), via Adaro Capital Limited, divested all its KCG shares and warrants (720,385,220 ordinary shares, equivalent to a 47.99% stake; one article reports 720.4 million shares), making Yancoal a 100% shareholder working with Mitsui, which retains 20%. Funding included company cash and an initial drawdown of a US$1.2 billion five-year syndicated acquisition loan, with contingent consideration of up to US$550 million (Rp9.85 trillion) if the coal benchmark price exceeds US$225 per ton in one of the first five years. ACL received US$814.12 million before tax (about Rp14.6 trillion; one article states Rp14.57 trillion) or US$734.83 million after tax (Rp13.2 trillion; one article states Rp13.15 trillion), with the Adaro Group potentially gaining up to US$1.36 billion (Rp24.52 trillion) earmarked for Indonesian business development, dividends, and partial loan repayment. Yancoal will recognize its share of Kestrel's production, revenue, and profit from October 1, 2026 and plans to send a shareholder document by Nov 23, 2026. AADI said the transaction is material, exceeding 20% but below 50% of equity under POJK 17/2020 without requiring shareholder approval; proforma six-month operating profit to June 30, 2026 rose from US$666.54 million to US$744.95 million, while profit for the period slipped from US$524.43 million to US$523.55 million.

topics.topic: Astra Agro Lestari (AALI) interim dividend of Rp233 per share
topics.known_state: PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) will distribute an interim dividend for fiscal year 2026 totaling Rp449.02 billion, or Rp233 per share, approved by the board of commissioners on 29 September 2026—its highest interim dividend since 2018, equal to a 40.86% payout of H1 2026 net profit of Rp1.10 trillion (reported as Rp1.09 trillion in one article), which was up 56.51% YoY. Based on financial data as of 30 June 2026 with unrestricted retained earnings of Rp18.99 trillion, the cum date in the regular and negotiation markets is 8 October 2026, the record date is 12 October at 4:00 PM WIB, and payment is scheduled for 26 October 2026.

topics.topic: Mitra Investindo (MITI) MoU with CNEC INA on silica sand mining concessions
topics.known_state: PT Mitra Investindo Tbk (MITI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding on 29 September 2026 with PT CNEC Engineering Indonesia, a subsidiary of China Nuclear Engineering & Construction Corporation, to develop three silica sand mining concessions held by MITI's subsidiaries, spanning exploration, feasibility studies, and technical engineering, with potential funding support.

topics.topic: Semancom (SEMA) clarification on CGK5 and CGK7 data center contracts
topics.known_state: PT Semacom Integrated Tbk (SEMA) clarified to the IDX that the CGK5 and CGK7 hyperscale data center contracts at Suryacipta Industrial Estate, Subang, West Java, are purely commercial supply agreements with Semacom appointed as supplier of Power Train Units (PTU) and SKIDs, with no affiliation to the contracting party, whose identity and contract value remain confidential under an NDA. Revenue, net income, and cash flow will be recognized gradually per milestones. Semacom cited data center construction costs of US$6.6 million to US$11.2 million per MW in Indonesia (midpoint US$8.3 million per MW per Cushman & Wakefield, converted at the JISDOR rate of Rp17,877 per US dollar on 30 September 2026), implying hypothetical construction costs of roughly Rp1.18 trillion to Rp10.01 trillion for 10 MW to 50 MW facilities.

topics.topic: Indonesia Stock Exchange reopening of short selling on October 1, 2026
topics.known_state: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) officially reopened short selling on Thursday, October 1, 2026, in a phased implementation limited to five large-capitalization stocks through two exchange members, PT Semesta Indovest Sekuritas and PT Ajaib Sekuritas Asia. The eligible stocks are ASII, BBCA, BRPT, BUMI, and INDF, selected with reference to the LQ45 index. Investors must open a special short selling account, have held a regular account (RDN) for at least six months, and meet a minimum initial capital requirement of Rp50 million.

topics.topic: IDX trading suspension of SMMT, BSWD, SONA, TEBE, and ASPI
topics.known_state: The Indonesia Stock Exchange suspended trading in PT Golden Eagle Energy Tbk (SMMT), PT Bank Of India Indonesia Tbk (BSWD), PT Sona Topas Tourism Industry Tbk (SONA), PT Dana Brata Luhur Tbk (TEBE), and PT Andalan Sakti Primaindo Tbk (ASPI) effective the October 1, 2026 session on the Regular and Cash Markets until further notice, citing significant cumulative price increases. Before the suspension, BSWD hit ARA three straight days (rising 24.92% to Rp1,855, 24.53% to Rp2,310, and 24.68% to Rp2,880 on September 28-30); SONA rose 24.69% to Rp2,980, 18.46% to Rp3,530, and 19.83% to Rp4,230 over the same days; ASPI gained 22.06% to Rp830 and 18.07% to Rp980 on September 29-30; TEBE rose 14.96% to Rp2,690 on September 30 after a 7.34% gain; and SMMT rose 0.86% to Rp3,520 on September 30 after an 11.82% jump to Rp3,500 on September 28.

topics.topic: Adhi Karya (ADHI) divestment of Jasamarga Jogja Solo and Dumai Tirta Persada stakes
topics.known_state: PT Adhi Karya (Persero) Tbk (ADHI) signed conditional share purchase agreements (reported as signed on 30 September 2026) to divest stakes in two subsidiaries for a combined Rp1.9 trillion (also stated as Rp1.91 trillion). ADHI will sell shares in PT Jasamarga Jogja Solo (JMJ)—reported as 1.7 million shares representing 41.18% in one article and 1,714,808 shares equal to 47.18% in another—to PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (Persero) for Rp1.76 trillion (Rp1,765,816,000,000; one article states Rp1.77 trillion), a material transaction requiring shareholder approval at an RUPSLB; JMJ is a BUJT formed by a consortium of Jasa Marga and ADHI, which won the Solo-Yogyakarta-NYIA Kulon Progo toll road tender, signing a PPJT with BPJT on September 9, 2020. ADHI will also sell 74,353 shares, or 51% of PT Dumai Tirta Persada, to PT Futura Energi Global Tbk (FUTR) for Rp141 billion, a non-material transaction under POJK No. 17/2020. Both transactions are not yet effective and are expected to be settled by 30 November 2026, after which ADHI will receive Rp1.91 trillion before tax and related costs. The divestments are part of ADHI's liquidity improvement program, which also targets three hotel assets operated by its subsidiaries.

topics.topic: Visi Media Asia (VIVA) net profit plunge of 95%
topics.known_state: Visi Media Asia (VIVA), a Bakrie Group issuer, reported net profit of Rp65.57 billion, a 95% drop from Rp1.19 trillion a year earlier, with basic EPS falling to Rp3,983 from Rp72,460. Revenue declined to Rp441.44 billion from Rp477.94 billion, and operating loss widened to Rp17.37 billion from Rp16.73 billion, driven in part by foreign exchange losses that grew to Rp50.06 billion from Rp16.97 billion. Total equity rose to Rp496.1 billion from Rp361.61 billion, while total assets slipped to Rp6.33 trillion from Rp6.38 trillion.

topics.topic: Selamat Sempurna (SMSM) dividend from subsidiary Bradke Synergies
topics.known_state: PT Selamat Sempurna Tbk (SMSM) announced receipt on 30 September of a MYR3,500,000 dividend from its subsidiary Bradke Synergies Sdn. Bhd., which at an estimated exchange rate of Rp4,390 per Malaysian Ringgit is expected to bring in approximately Rp15.36 billion, with no negative impact on the company's operations, legal standing, financial condition, or business continuity.

topics.topic: Japfa Comfeed (JPFA) divestment of 100% of Vaksindo to Japfa Pte Ltd and Bionovus
topics.known_state: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk (JPFA), together with subsidiary PT Ciomas Adisatwa, sold its entire 100% stake (31,000 shares) in PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara, along with the VAKSINDO, VAKSIMUNE, and VITAKUR trademarks, to Japfa Pte Ltd and Bionovus in a transaction valued at Rp1.80 trillion (also stated as Rp1,807 trillion, with a headline figure of Rp1.81 trillion), effective 29 September 2026 with payment due that date. Japfa Pte Ltd is JPFA's controlling shareholder with a 56.34% stake, making it an affiliated transaction, though the company stated it is not a conflict-of-interest transaction under POJK 42/2020 and not material under POJK 17/POJK.04/2020; the value equals 8.47% of JPFA's consolidated equity as of 30 June 2026, and an independent appraisal by KJPP Ruky, Safrudin & Rekan valued 100% of Vaksindo and its subsidiaries at Rp1,807 trillion. After the transaction JPFA will no longer consolidate Vaksindo's revenue, profit, and assets, including subsidiaries in India and Vietnam, while livestock raw material supply relations are expected to continue on substantially the same terms.

topics.topic: Bank Syariah Indonesia (BRIS) rights issue plan (PMHMETD II)
topics.known_state: PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BRIS) plans a rights issue of up to 6.8 billion new Series B shares with a nominal value of Rp500 per share to strengthen capital and expand financing capacity; the exercise price and final share count will be disclosed in the prospectus. Proceeds after issuance costs will be used entirely to expand financing distribution, with equity projected to rise from Rp51.07 trillion in 2026 to Rp64.41 trillion in 2027 and the CAR expected to increase from 20.38% to 23.31%; shareholders who do not exercise face dilution of up to 12.85%. The plan requires shareholder approval at an RUPSLB on Friday, 6 November 2026, with completion targeted in Q1 2027, subject to OJK effective registration.

topics.topic: Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BBRI) January-August 2026 net profit
topics.known_state: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) recorded net profit of Rp34.77 trillion for January to August 2026, with pre-tax profit of Rp42.57 trillion and net interest income of Rp77.25 trillion. CASA stood at about 64.8% of third-party funds, with an estimated cost of fund of around 2.9% and cost of credit of roughly 3.1% annually. Savings of Rp623.72 trillion, demand deposits of Rp449.36 trillion, and time deposits of Rp582.74 trillion brought total DPK to about Rp1,655.84 trillion, while total loans reached Rp1,446.98 trillion, about 87% of DPK. The bank holds impairment allowance reserves of Rp77.09 trillion, total assets of Rp2,127.78 trillion, and paid dividends of Rp52.10 trillion, against industry DPK growth of 10.94% and credit growth of 13.65% as of August 2026.

topics.topic: Telkom Indonesia spin-off of fiber network business to InfraNexia
topics.known_state: PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk's extraordinary general meeting on September 30, 2026 approved, with independent shareholder approval, the spin-off of its wholesale fiber connectivity business and assets to subsidiary PT Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia (Telkom InfraCo/TIF), known as InfraNexia. The transaction is valued at Rp85.7 trillion (one report states cumulative transaction value of around Rp49.9 trillion) and transfers more than 90 percent of Telkom's network infrastructure assets, including 112,000 kilometers of fiber optic cable with 26,000 kilometers of inter-island submarine cable. The spin-off is part of the TLKM 30 strategy, positioning Telkom as a Strategic Holding and InfraNexia as a carrier-neutral, open-access network infrastructure operator, consolidating fiber connectivity into TIF ahead of a potential transaction with a strategic partner.

topics.topic: Bank JTrust Indonesia (BCIC) H1 2026 financial results
topics.known_state: PT Bank JTrust Indonesia Tbk (BCIC) posted H1 2026 net profit of Rp80.23 billion, with loans growing 8.59% to Rp29.25 trillion from Rp26.94 trillion at end-2025, net NPL improving to 1.78% from 2.26%, total assets reaching Rp39.83 trillion, and third-party funds up 1.08% to Rp33.92 trillion. Cost of funds was optimized at 4.69% as of June 2026, down from 5.27% at end-2025. Total capital rose to Rp3.71 trillion from Rp3.15 trillion and the capital adequacy ratio increased to 14.53% from 12.53%. The bank plans to push fee-based income and syndicated loans, increase low-cost funds, and modernize its core banking system.

topics.topic: Telkom Indonesia RUPSLB replaces President Director Dian Siswarini with Nanang Hendarno
topics.known_state: An extraordinary general meeting of shareholders of PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk on 30 September 2026 replaced President Director Dian Siswarini, who had held the post since 27 May 2025, with Nanang Hendarno, previously Director Network. Other changes: Budi Satria Dharma Purba became Director Network, Radita Ali Putra took the Director Wholesale & International Service role, and Kharim I. G. Siregar replaced Faizal R. Djoemadi as Director IT Digital. The company stated the change has no material impact on operational, legal, or financial activities, and no official reason was given, though sources suggested it may relate to internal reforms Dian initiated, including addressing alleged conflicts of interest and scrutiny over infrastructure capex of Rp20 trillion for Telkom and Rp15 trillion for Telkomsel.

topics.topic: City Retail Developments (NIRO) divestment of seven subsidiaries for Rp1.33 trillion
topics.known_state: PT City Retail Developments Tbk (NIRO) will divest 100% ownership in seven indirect subsidiaries—PT Cella Management Logistik, PT Cella Argya Logistik, PT Bukit Inti Lestari, PT CRE BIL Indonesia, PT Cella Cakra Logistik, PT Cella Emerald Logistik, and PT Cella Gemilang Logistik—for Rp1.33 trillion, equivalent to 29.44% of its equity of Rp4.53 trillion as of June 30, 2026, making it a material transaction under POJK 17/POJK.04/2020. The price is 0.10% above the KJPP FDI&R appraisal of Rp1,332 trillion, which deemed it fair. The divestment addresses liquidity, working capital, and funding needs, lifting proforma cash and equivalents from Rp1.23 trillion to Rp2.39 trillion and cutting the proforma current-period loss from Rp237.59 billion to Rp36.25 billion via a Rp201.34 billion divestment gain; impacts on revenue and operating cash flow are projected to emerge after 2027, amid NIRO's current ratio of 0.70x and debt-to-equity ratio of 1.95x as of June 30, 2026.

topics.topic: GOTO price discovery phase after removal of Rp50 minimum price floor
topics.known_state: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) entered a new price discovery phase after its shares were no longer bound by the Rp50 minimum price floor, with selling pressure of around 1 billion lots per day in early trading and shares falling to Rp28 in the first session on Thursday (1/10/2026), following GOTO's removal from the MSCI and FTSE indexes with passive fund outflows of roughly 116 billion shares, about 10% of shares outstanding. GOTO posted a first-half 2026 net profit of Rp607 billion on net revenue of Rp10.99 trillion, with Q2-2026 net revenue of Rp5.7 trillion and adjusted Group EBITDA surpassing Rp1 trillion for the first time. CEO Hans Patuwo said the company is considering a reverse stock split and plans to cancel treasury shares, while ensuring macroeconomic conditions are right before deploying its previously announced Rp3.5 trillion buyback funds; management targets full-year 2026 adjusted Group EBITDA of Rp3.2-3.4 trillion.

topics.topic: AirAsia Indonesia (CMPP) negative equity restoration options and trading suspension
topics.known_state: PT AirAsia Indonesia Tbk (CMPP) is evaluating three options to restore its negative equity, which triggered the IDX to suspend trading of its shares on 30 June 2026: converting trade payables and lease liabilities owed to its controlling entity or shareholders into perpetual or semi-equity instruments, a rights issue (PMHMETD), and a private placement or non-pre-emptive capital increase (PMTHMETD), with no final decision made. As of 30 June 2026, the capital deficit reached Rp12.19 trillion, up from Rp10.74 trillion at end-December 2025. In H1 2026, the company posted a net loss of Rp1.45 trillion, widening from Rp785.84 billion in H1 2025, while revenue fell 1.78% to Rp3,905 trillion.

topics.topic: Mitra Keluarga (MIKA) H1 2026 results and 2026 growth targets
topics.known_state: PT Mitra Keluarga Karyasehat Tbk (MIKA) posted H1 2026 revenue of about Rp2.7 trillion (Rp2.77 trillion per one article), up 8% YoY, with net profit of Rp684 billion, up 6.9%. High-complexity services revenue grew 28.6% to Rp767 billion, raising its contribution to 27.7% of total revenue (28% per one article) from 23.2% a year earlier; private patients accounted for 90% of total patients/revenue, JKN revenue fell 11.4% YoY, gross margin slipped to 53.4% from 54.7%, and average revenue per inpatient day rose 12.2% to Rp4.68 million. The company targets around 10% performance growth for fiscal 2026 (2026 revenue growth guidance in the low-to-mid teens per one article) while maintaining an EBITDA margin of 38.8%-39.5%, and plans new hospitals in BSD (operational Q4-2026) and East Java (Q1-2027), plus a nuclear medicine center and integrated oncology platform in East Java, funded by a net cash position of about Rp3 trillion with no debt.

topics.topic: Wijaya Karya (WIKA) debt restructuring of securities and bank debt in 2026
topics.known_state: PT Wijaya Karya Tbk (WIKA) is seeking approval from holders of its debt securities to restructure Rp10.2 trillion in debt securities throughout 2026, while banking restructuring is targeted at Rp17.6 trillion in 2026, with agreements hoped to be reached by end-2026 alongside RUPO and RUPSU meetings on yield payment terms. The restructuring proposal includes divestments totaling Rp5 trillion during 2026-2028, with subsidiaries returning proceeds to WIKA as shareholder loan repayments to settle debt securities and bank obligations, plus a streamlining program targeting returns of at least 8% for joint operation projects and above 10% for regular projects.

topics.topic: President Prabowo Red and White Cabinet reshuffle
topics.known_state: President Prabowo Subianto reshuffled the Red and White Cabinet: Police General Listyo Sigit Prabowo was appointed Presidential Chief of Staff, replacing TNI General Dudung Abdurachman; Police General Suyudi Ario Seto became Kapolri; and Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia moved to Coordinating Minister for Downstreaming and Energy.

topics.topic: VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas revenue growth on commercial EV sales
topics.known_state: PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR) reported net sales of Rp648 billion, up 56% YoY, driven by growth in its commercial electric vehicle business and spare parts manufacturing segment. Operating profit rose 1,782% YoY to Rp15 billion, while net profit reached Rp10 billion, up 25% YoY. As of end-June 2026, total assets stood at Rp1.8 trillion, with liabilities of Rp561 billion and equity of Rp1.2 trillion. The company is developing an Electric Mobility-as-a-Service (e-MaaS) leasing model to shift customer spending from CAPEX to OPEX across public transport, logistics, plantation, industrial, and mining sectors.
